title: I fully vibecoded this terrain painter. One noise texture, everything else is code. Now free for Godot.
author: idlerunner00
selftext:
This started as terrain for a game prototype I was vibecoding in three.js. I ended up turning it into its own tool.

I used Claude Code and Codex to port it to Godot/C#, extracted the terrain system, and built a standalone studio around it. It’s now **Cartoon Terrain Studio**, free and open source under the MIT license.

The cliffs, trees, rivers, waterfalls and cartoon materials are all generated through code and shaders. The only texture input is a single noise lookup.

You can paint a map from scratch, generate one and edit it by hand, or explore an endless world from a seed. You can also change the whole look live, including colours, lighting, seasons and weather.

[**Get the tool and source on GitHub**](https://github.com/idlerunner00/cartoon-terrain-studio)

On Windows, download the ZIP, extract it and double-click `Start.cmd`. It downloads Godot and a local .NET SDK if needed, builds the project and launches the studio.

The wildest part of this project is how much AI improved while I was building it. About three months ago, I started experimenting with procedural terrain in three.js for a game prototype. Getting that first version looking and behaving the way I wanted took a LOT of iteration. If I started again today, with current models and what I’ve learned, I’d bet I could get that original terrain working in a weekend, maybe even a single day.

For anyone building with AI: the generation logic is separated from the Godot renderer, and the repo includes an architecture guide. If you want to bring the terrain into your own game, there is a starting prompt for a coding agent with access to your project:

    Integrate the terrain system from this repository into my game:
    https://github.com/idlerunner00/cartoon-terrain-studio
    
    My engine and version: [ENGINE / VERSION]
    My project: [EXISTING PROJECT PATH, OR DESCRIBE A NEW PROJECT]
    Features I want: [GENERATED MAPS / ENDLESS WORLDS / TERRAIN PAINTING / A SINGLE EXPORTED MAP OR STYLE]
    
    Read the repository's README.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, then inspect my project before making changes. Identify the terrain generation, mesh building, vegetation, materials and rendering components needed for these features. Reuse the existing implementation and preserve its visual style.
    For Godot, integrate the relevant C# code, shaders and resources. For another engine, identify which parts can be reused and which require porting. Ensure a fully usable port. Start with a runnable scene containing generated terrain, a camera and lighting. Then connect it to my project, following its existing architecture and preserving unrelated functionality. Include the noise texture and all required shader dependencies. Keep generation deterministic for a given seed. Expose the seed and relevant terrain/style settings. Only include the studio's editing UI if my requested features need it.
    Implement the integration, build and run it, and fix any errors you encounter. Finish with setup instructions, the controls/settings you added, and anything still unverified.
